title: Communication durable event envelope
description: Envelope for every row of the `domain_events` journal and every `data:` frame of the project SSE stream (communication-spec/09-api-events-data.md, 'Durable event envelope'). Identifiers are Postgres `uuid` values rendered as strings; timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC. `global_seq` is the monotonic replay cursor used for SSE `Last-Event-ID` / `?after=`. The envelope is stable; the shape of `payload` is defined per event `type` and per `schema_version` by the event type's own schema.

event_id.description: Stable unique id of this event (`uuidv7()` at insert time). Distinct from `global_seq`, which is the ordering cursor.

global_seq.description: Database-generated global sequence (`bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`). Monotonic; the SSE event `id:` and the reconnect cursor.

type.description: Dotted lowercase event type, e.g. `project.created`, `repository.added`, `node.attempt.completed`. First segment admits underscores for ADR-0049's `node_template.*` names.

schema_version.description: Version of the payload schema for this `type`. Consumers must ignore payload fields they do not know.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the state transition.

organization_id.description: Owning organization. Every journal row is organization scoped.

project_id.description: Project the event belongs to; null for organization-wide events. Gates the per-project SSE subscription.

conversation_id.description: Conversation the event belongs to, when it is conversation-scoped (M2, ADR-0016: the transcript is this journal read through `conversation_id`). Null otherwise. A conversation-scoped row always carries `project_id` too, so the project stream remains a superset and one gap-safe cursor serves both.

run_id.description: Run the event belongs to, when it is run-scoped (M4, docs/m4-contract.md § 1/§ 3: the `domain_events.run_id` column, indexed `(run_id, global_seq)`, which is what `GET /api/v1/runs/{runId}/events` streams through). Additive per ADR-0014 § 8 — consumers ignore members they do not know. A run-scoped row always carries `project_id` too. Null on every pre-M4 row and on non-run events.

node_execution_id.description: Node execution the event is about (§ 3's correlation rule). A worker row that touches a node execution sets this AND `attempt_id`; a control-plane row may carry this with `attempt_id` null, because control-plane work creates no attempts (ADR-0023 § 3).

attempt_id.description: Attempt the event is about (`domain_events.attempt_id`, indexed `(attempt_id, global_seq)`). Set on every attempt-lifecycle event, written under the row's fence; null for control-plane events, which have no attempts.

actor.description: Who caused the transition. `id` is the internal id for humans/agents/workers, an integration key for integrations, and the literal `system` for system actions.

trace_id.description: Optional distributed-trace id correlating the request, event and any downstream agent work. Omitted when absent.

payload.description: Event-specific detail, validated by the schema registered for (`type`, `schema_version`). Secrets appear here as metadata only (id/version/scope), never as material values.
